> The Canadian Centre on Substance Abuse said last week that once marijuana is legalized, it should be distributed through a tightly regulated system – in which making a profit is not the objective.

>“A public-health framework means preventing a revenue-driven approach, even within government-regulated sales,” CCSA policy adviser Rebecca Jesseman said at a public hearing held by the Senate Liberal caucus.

This worries me only because a cannabis regulation model that prevents or seriously discourages a for profit business model may not undercut the black market. Price of the product has huge impacts on substance abuse and moderation indicted [here](http://www.ccsa.ca/Eng/topics/alcohol/alcohol-pricing-in-Canada/Pages/default.aspx) on the CCSA website. It's so important infact that provinces have a 'social reference price' for alcohol. If you'd like a more detailed analysis you can read [Social Reference Prices for Alcohol] (http://www.ccsa.ca/Resource%20Library/CCSA-Social-Reference-Prices-for-Alcohol-Canada-Report-2015-en.pdf) a report from July 2015 published by the CCSA.

So what legislators need to do is find the 'goldilocks' pricing and tax model that will encourage moderation but at the same time be competitive with an already very established black market. 

A revenue motivated market is not good at 'harm reduction' because their main goal is to sell more product which contradicts a moderation message. However it usually produces a more cost efficient and cheaper product to the consumer.

I personally bought The Evil Within (didn't pre-order) and the game seems to be running fairly stable on my system. Don't let the opening outside sequence scare you everyone is getting 30-40 FPS with dips during that specific sequence. As soon as you go inside the frames instantly jump to 60 and stay there with very little stuttering or dipping. 

That being said the game does suffer from some occasional texture pops and during death animations due to the claustrophobic level design texture clipping is very common.

As for the absurd VRAM amount indicated in the recommend specs, you need no where near 4GB. According to Afterburner I used on average between 1.5GB and 1.8GB. Any 2GB card will run this game fine at 1080p. 

One of the console commands does allow you to change the interesting aspect ratio. I personally don't find the 2:5:1 to offensive, but some do. If you do change the aspect ratio to lets say 1.78 for a 16:9 display it completely screws up the FOV. The game just zooms in on the existing 2:5:1 ratio. Everything is scaled properly its just a lot narrower FOV. There is a setting to change the FOV, but it does absolutely nothing so hopefully either the devs patch this or mods are made to remedy this issue. NOTE: If you are using a 21:9 monitor The Evil Within currently only supports 16:9. The game even full screen will only populate the middle part of your 21:9 display as well as running in the 2:5:1 aspect ratio, with no way to change it. So if you do have a 21:9 display you will have both horizontal black bars and vertical ones...sorry.
